label: prop:three-strand-color-winding-rigidity
title: Rigidity of the three-strand color winding: $(\sigma_1\sigma_2)^3 = \mathrm{Id}$ on the $(2,1)$ block, $q$-independently
html:
On the 2-dimensional (2,1) Hoefsmit block of H_3(q), the uniform three-strand rotation M = \rho_{(2,1)}(\sigma_1\sigma_2) has

\mathrm{tr}\,M = -1, \qquad \det M = 1, \qquad M^3 = \mathrm{Id},

for every q with 1 - q^2 invertible. The eigenvalues of M are the primitive cube roots of unity, independently of q.

The proof is Cayley–Hamilton: trace -1 and determinant 1 give the \zeta_3 quadratic M^2 = -M - 1, hence M^3 = \mathrm{Id}. The trace identity is a Laurent identity in q alone; the determinant identity is exactly the Hoefsmit constraint \beta^2 = a_2 a_{-2} + 1 on the binding amplitude (prop:hoefsmit-binding-amplitude). The Lean sibling states both over a generic commutative ring with q a unit and with both \beta and the axial entry a_2 carried as constrained variables — \beta^2 = a_{-2} a_2 + 1 and a_2 (1 - q^4) = q - q^{-1} — so neither the square root nor the axial-distance quotient appears (no division, no \mathbb{R}), and derives the cube identity from the two scalar facts. Only the trace needs 1 - q^2 invertible, and genuinely so: at q^2 = 1 the defining relation for a_2 degenerates and constrains nothing. The determinant identity needs no hypothesis at all.

Since the closures of (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^k are the (3,k) torus links, the proposition says the compact winding of the three-strand torus-link tower is topological: a \zeta_3 (color/triality) rotation that does not flow with the substrate modulus, in contrast to the modulus-carrying hyperbolic winding pair q^{\pm 2k} of the 1-dimensional channels. The level-lattice and vortex readings — winding pair (k,\ k \bmod 3) for the three-strand (Borromean/nucleon) carrier, and the alternating-word deformation of the same rotation — are developed in the channel- interpolation cross-check and its witnesses (toroidal-level-selection-three-strand-probe, alternating-tower-borromean-winding-probe).
